t: You're at Birkbeck, University of London, in Bloomsbury. It was established in 1823 as the London Mechanics' Institute, and it is one of the few universities in the United Kingdom to specialise in evening higher education. George Birkbeck, the physician and pioneer in adult education, is the man whose name it carries. He is known for creating mechanics' institutes in Scotland and London. His supporters included Jeremy Bentham, J. C. Hobhouse and Henry Brougham, and its founder was Joseph Clinton Robertson.
